The stem frames the inference as a supposition and dense patches can divert flow, so not logged as a fact error, but worth a coordinator look. items.cold_note: Distance-matched pair: M 2.0 km vs F 1.6 km (0.4 km apart), conductivity 164 vs 41. But D (R 3.2 vs J 4.5) is defensible: J is FARTHER yet far lower (152 vs 63 June), so a distance explanation predicts the opposite of what is seen - arguably a stronger test, since in C the B spring is closer and its lower value could be read as a distance effect.

second_defensible.reason: R (Unit C, 3.2 km) vs J (Unit B, 4.5 km): J is farther from the glacier yet has far lower conductivity (63 vs 152 June, 47 vs 131 Aug). Among Unit B springs conductivity rises with distance, so a distance explanation predicts J > R; the opposite result isolates rock unit. In the key pair the Unit B spring (F) is the closer one, so its lower value runs in the direction distance would also predict. The key rests on the closest-distance convention; D is a sound test from the same table.
